articles.title: Prayagraj hosts 41st Indira Marathon on Indira Gandhi's birth anniversary - Awaz The Voice
articles.content: The 41st All India Prize Money Indira Marathon and Half Marathon was organised in Prayagraj on Friday to commemorate the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Indira Gandhi, India's first woman Prime Minister, was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, now Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. She was the daughter of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. Speaking on the sidelines of the event to reporters, Prayagraj Police Commissioner Piyush Mordia said extensive security and traffic arrangements have been put in place for the marathon to ensure the safety and convenience of participants. Police personnel have been deployed along the route, with ambulances and police vehicles accompanying the runners. He added that the event is being continuously monitored through CCTV cameras from the Integrated Command and Control Centre until its conclusion. “The police make arrangements every year to ensure that runners do not face any inconvenience along the route. No traffic is allowed on the side of the divider reserved for marathon runners, while traffic operates only on the other side. The entire left side is kept clear for the participants... Police personnel have been deployed at every intersection and turn along the route, and their duty will continue until the marathon concludes. A police vehicle is leading the runners, while ambulances and police personnel are accompanying them from behind... Police personnel at the Integrated Command and Control Centre are continuously monitoring the event through CCTV cameras. Monitoring will continue without interruption until the marathon is over," Mordia said. Prayagraj Divisional Commissioner Lokesh M said the event has attracted around 1,000 participants across different categories. He added that the annual event, organised for the past 41 years, is being conducted by the Uttar Pradesh government's Sports Department this year. “This is the 41st Indira Marathon, featuring two events: a full marathon of 42 kilometres and a half marathon of 21 kilometres. Athletes from different categories are participating, with around 1,000 participants in total. The half marathon has the larger number of participants... This event has been organised every year for the past 41 years. This year, it is being organised by the state government's Sports Department, " Lokesh M said. While, Prayagraj District Magistrate Manish Kumar Verma said the 21-km half marathon was reintroduced this year following a request from the women's group Prayagraj Pacers, with encouraging participation from women. He added that the prize money remains unchanged, with the full marathon winner set to receive Rs 2 lakh, while the half marathon winners will receive Rs 51,000, Rs 21,000 and Rs 11,000, respectively. articles.title: Gaganyaan Mission Launch Sriharikota; Indian Astronauts Travel March 2028
articles.content: English News National Gaganyaan Mission Launch Sriharikota; Indian Astronauts Travel March 2028 ISRO eyes December-January Gaganyaan launch: No humanoid robot on first mission, astronauts to fly in March 2028 Anirudh Sharma, New Delhi 11 hours ago Copy link If the first two flights are successful, Indian astronauts will travel to space on the third flight by March 2028. Preparations for the first uncrewed flight (G-1) of India's first human space mission, 'Gaganyaan', are in the final stage. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh told Bhaskar on Wednesday that the launch is being planned for the end of December or the beginning of January 2027. He said the flight, which will take off from the second launch pad at Sriharikota, will carry the crew and service modules into space. Its main objective is to test the safe return of the crew module. The humanoid robot 'Vyommitra' will not be sent on the first flight but on the second. If the first two flights are successful, Indian astronauts will travel into space on the third flight by March 2028. Once the mission is completed, India will become the fourth country after the United States, Russia and China to send humans into space. It is expected to be launched using the first human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3) rocket. Three phases of the mission: Only one or two tests remain Rocket and testing: The mission will be launched on the human-rated HLMV-3 rocket. This is an upgraded version of the rocket used for Chandrayaan-3. At present, the entire module is undergoing thermo-vacuum testing. The equipment is being examined in vacuum conditions similar to those in space. Gaganyaan has passed the test for separating the modules ISRO has completed testing of the system for separating the crew module (CM) and service module (SM) of the Gaganyaan programme. This has confirmed the design capability of the system. These tests were conducted on 16 October this year at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) in Thiruvananthapuram. Understand module separation through questions and answers... Why is it necessary to separate the modules: The Gaganyaan crew module has to return to Earth, while the service module provides essential services in space. The service module must be separated during the return journey so that the crew module can re-enter the atmosphere with its own heat shield. Power and fluid connections will also separate: Umbilical connections link the two modules for power, communications and environmental control, as well as fluids connected to the life-support system. These connections must also break in the correct sequence during separation. The heat shield will protect against intense heat: The crew module will face intense heat while re-entering the Earth's atmosphere. A thermal protection system and heat shield are essential for this. A recent test also assessed the shock resistance of the components associated with them. The goal is not just to reach space, but also to return safely: Parachutes will play a crucial role in the crew module's return. They help reduce the module's speed, enabling safe recovery...

articles.title: CIAL operationalises India's first transfer cargo security hold area - The New Indian Express
articles.content: KOCHI: Cochin International Airport Ltd (CIAL) has operationalised India’s first Transfer Cargo Security Hold Area (TCSHA) to speed up the movement of cargo between domestic and international destinations through Kochi. Chief Minister V D Satheesan inaugurated the facility on Wednesday. The TCSHA facility will expedite cargo movement by enabling the transfer of consignments between domestic and international flights entirely within the airport’s operational area. Earlier, transfer cargo had to be moved to the cargo terminal for repeat security screening before being brought back to the airside cargo area for loading onto the connecting flight. The facility is expected to reduce transfer cargo screening requirements to random 5 %, helping cut transit time and handling costs. Under the earlier system, domestic cargo arriving at Kochi for onward transportation to international destinations could take up to three days to complete the transfer process, as it had to undergo repeated handling procedures and 100% security re-screening. The new facility, developed near the airport’s operational area, allows transfer cargo to be moved to connecting international flights in hours, with only 5% subjected to randomized screening at the facility. This is expected to significantly reduce cargo dwell time.
